Date : 22/09/2017  ORAL JUDGMENT HC-NIC Page 1 of 6 Created On Mon Oct 02 03:32:30 IST 2017 R/CR.RA/1001/2016 JUDGMENT [1.0] Feeling aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and order passed by the learned Principal Sessions Judge, Sabarkantha at Himatnagar dated 14/12/2016 in Criminal Appeal No.32/2009 by which the learned appellate Court has partly allowed the said Appeal and has confirmed the order of conviction passed by the learned trial Court convicting the original accused for the offence punishable under Section 7(1) and 7(5) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act,
1954 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act") and has sentenced the original accused to undergo 1 year Simple Imprisonment with fine of Rs.1000/- (each) and in default to undergo further 5 days Simple Imprisonment, however, the learned appellate Court has modified the order of sentence and has sentenced the original accused to undergo six months Simple Imprisonment with the fine maintained by the learned trial Court
, original accused have preferred the present Criminal Revision Application.
[2.0] It is not in dispute that charge against the petitioners - original accused was only of sub standardization of the goods.

[3.0] Shri J.V. Japee, learned advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners has submitted that though all the accused have some case even on merits, he would be giving up the plea on merits and his only submission is about sentence imposed by the Courts below.
He has requested to consider the subsequent amendment in the Act by the Central Amendment Act whereby Sections 51 and 52 have been added and under the said Sections, only fine is to be imposed.
HC-NIC Page 2 of 6 Created On Mon Oct 02 03:32:30
R/CR.RA/1001/2016 JUDGM
Therefore, he has requested to maintain conviction but modify the sentence and impose fine only.

[3.1] In support of his above submissions and in support of his above request, Shri J.V. Japee,
learned advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners - original accused has heavily relied upon the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Nemi Chand vs. State of Rajasthan dated 17/03/2016 passed in Criminal Appeal No.214 of 2016.

sentences.text: [[4.1] Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and more particularly the fact that charge is only of sub- standardization of goods and request is made by learned advocate appearing for the petitioners and considering the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Nemi Chand (supra), she has requested to pass appropriate order.

[5.0] Having heard Shri J.V. Japee, learned advocate appearing for the petitioners and Ms. C.M.
Shah, learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing on behalf of respondent no.1 and considering the facts and circumstances of the case, more particularly, when the charge against the petitioners is only of sub standardization of the goods and that original accused was convicted for the offence under under Section 7(1) and 7(5) of the Act and has sentenced the original accused to undergo 1 year Simple Imprisonment with fine of Rs.1000/- (each) and in default to undergo further 5 days Simple Imprisonment, however, the learned appellate Court HC-NIC Page 3 of 6 Created On Mon Oct 02 03:32:30 IST 2017 R/CR.RA/1001/2016 JUDGMENT has modified the order of sentence and has sentenced the original accused to undergo six months Simple Imprisonment with the fine maintained by the learned trial Court, considering the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Nemi Chand (Supra) and amendment in the Act by Central Amendment Act 34 of 1976 whereby Sections 51 and 52 have been added and under said Sections only fine is leviable, decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Nemi Chand (supra) squarely applies.

[6.0] In the case of Nemi Chand, (supra), the Hon'ble Supreme Court has considered similar request and has observed as under:
"2.
It is not in dispute that the charge against the appellant was only of sub-standardization of goods.

Mr. Sushil Kumar Jain, learned senior counsel appearing for the appellant, submits that though the appellant has some prima facie case even on merits, he would be giving up the plea on merits and his only submission is about the sentence which has been imposed by the courts below.
He has, in this behalf, argued that there has been an amendment in the Act by the Central Amendment Act 34 of 1976 whereby Section 16A was added and under the said section, only a fine is leviable.

He has drawn our attention to the judgment of this Court in "T. Barai V. Henry Ah Hoe and Another" [1983 (1) SCC 177] wherein this Court held that since the amendment was beneficial to the accused persons, it can be applied even with respect to earlier cases as well which are pending in the Court.

entities.text: T. Barai V. Henry Ah Hoe and Another" [1983 (1) SCC 177]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the said judgment, the Court held as under :-
"22.
It is only retroactive criminal legislation that is prohibited under Article 20(1).

The prohibition contained in Article 20(1) is that no person shall be convicted of any offence except for violation of a law in force at the time of the HC-NIC Page 4 of 6 Created On Mon Oct 02 03:32:30 IST 2017 R/CR.RA/1001/2016 JUDGMENT commission of the act charged as an offence prohibits nor shall he be subjected to a penalty greater than that which might have been inflicted under the law in force at the time of the commission of the offence.

It is quite clear that insofar as the Central Amendment Act creates new offences or enhances punishment for a particular type of offence no person can be convicted by such ex post facto law nor can the enhanced Aazambhai Miyaahmed Valjivala & vs State Of Gujarat on 22 September, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90099258/
3 punishment prescribed by the amendment be applicable.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But insofar as the Central Amendment Act reduces the punishment for an offence punishable under Section 16(1)(a) of the Act, there is no reason why the accused should not have the benefit of such reduced punishment.
The rule of beneficial construction requires that even ex post facto law of such a type should be applied to mitigate the rigour of the law.
The principle is based both on sound reason and common sense.
This finds support in the following passage from Craies on Statute Law, 7th Edn., at pp. 388-89:
A retrospective statute is different from an ex post facto statute.

"Every ex post facto law...."
said Chase, J., in the American case of Calder v. Bull "must necessarily be retrospective, but every retrospective law is not an ex post facto law.

Every law that takes away or impairs rights vested agreeably to existing laws is retrospective, and is generally unjust and may be oppressive; it is a good general rule that a law should have no retrospect, but in cases in which the laws may justly and for the benefit of the community and also of individuals relate to a time antecedent to their commencement: as statutes of oblivion or of pardon.
They are certainly retrospective, and literally both concerning and after the facts committed.

But I HC-NIC Page 5 of 6 Created On Mon Oct 02 03:32:30 IST 2017 R/CR.RA/1001/2016 JUDGMENT do not consider any law ex post facto within the prohibition that mollifies the rigour of the criminal law, but only those that create or aggravate the crime, or increase the punishment or change the rules of evidence for the purpose of conviction....
There is a great and apparent difference between making an unlawful act lawful and the making an innocent action criminal and punishing it as a crime."
From the facts of the present case, we have no doubt in mind that the aforesaid judgment squarely applies thereon.
This appeal is, therefore, partly allowed and the sentence imposed upon the appellant is modified by imposing fine of Rs. 50,000/- which shall be deposited within two months with the trial court.
On deposit of the aforesaid amount, the bail bonds furnished by the appellant shall be discharged."
[7.0] Under the circumstances, present Criminal Revision Application is partly allowed.

The sentence imposed upon the petitioners by the learned trial Court confirmed by the learned appellate Court is hereby modified by imposing fine of Rs.25,000/- each, which shall be deposited before the learned trial court within a period of four weeks from today.

On deposit of the aforesaid amount,
bail bond furnished by the petitioners - original accused shall be discharged.
Rule is made absolute to the aforesaid extent.
Direct service is permitted.
